steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Place beaten egg in a shallow bowl. Place cornstarch and garlic salt into a large resealable plastic bag.
Dip chicken in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Drop chicken into cornstarch mixture, seal the bag, and shake until well coated.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook chicken in hot oil, turning occasionally, until browned, about 5 minutes. Transfer chicken to a baking dish.
Stir together vinegar, sugar, broth, ketchup, soy sauce, and salt in a medium bowl. Pour over chicken in the baking dish.

Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 40 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet and Sour Chicken Tenders
raw_recipe.description: These sweet and sour chicken tenders are pan-fried until crisp, then tossed in a tangy sauce of vinegar, broth, ketchup, and a hint of soy sauce.

review.reviewBody: Would add a few more ingredients such as onion,peppers etc

This was a very good recipe, 4 stars as is and 5 stars with a few changes. I doubled recipe as have more than 4 people to feed. I did not double apple cider vinegar tho, left it at 1/2 cup as other reviewers suggested. Added 1/4 cup pineapple juice and 1/2 of 14 Oz can chunked pineapples. Used 1/2 cup cornstarch and 1/2 cup flour to dip chicken in as others suggested. I omitted oven and cooked it all in a large skillet. After browning chicken (also added 1 diced red sweet pepper while browning chicken) I removed it to combine the sauce then added it back to the skillet to cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes. Sauce was a bit watery to me so I thickened it with a cornstarch and water mixture (approximately 3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1/4 cup cold water) at end of 15 mins.

I added pineapple chunks & the juice, onions, green peppers, escallion, hot pepper and corn starch to thicken the sauce. I cooked on the stovetop. It was so delicious and the recipe was easy to follow. I loved breading the tenderloins in cornstarch in lieu of flour. I cannot wait to eat my leftovers 😋

Really easy, really delicious sweet and sour chicken. My husband and I both thoroughly enjoyed this--not only for the flavor, but for the ease of making it. I deducted one star just because of the baking time: my chicken tenders were done in only 25 minutes--so that's something I'd definitely keep an eye on, depending on the size of your chicken tenders. I also used honey in place of sugar, and rice wine vinegar in place of cider vinegar. It was delicious! I will definitely be making this again. Thank you for the recipe!

Great recipe! I added one red pepper, one green pepper and 7 ounces of crushed pineapple from the can. I added the pineapple 30 minutes into baking and let it sit with the chicken for 10 minutes (total baking time was 40 min).

This recipe is amazing with a few minor adjustments. I double the sauce ingredients as there’s not enough to saturate the rice if you make it as is. HOWEVER, I do NOT double the vinegar as it can been too much. I cut the tenders into chunks before coating with cornstarch and I add 2 red peppers and a cup of pineapple chunks. I also do not cook in the oven. I just add the chicken back into the pan with the peppers & pineapples and then the sauce to finish cooking the chicken. Goes perfectly with basmati rice!
I left out the ketchup, only used 1/2 of the vinegar as suggested, and did it in one pan on stovetop. Very easy and good. It looked like far too much time in the oven and used more dishes!

This is a keeper! We made it all in the skillet. After browning the tenders, we set them aside and sauteed onions, green and red peppers, then returned the chicken to the pan and added a can of sliced water chestnuts, simmered about five minutes and served over quinoa and brown rice. It was delicious, no leftovers.

Came out great. I added chili powder, garlic powder,salt and onion powder to the corn starch. I used half vinegar as suggested and cooked it in a skillet instead of the oven. I know it would be crispier in the oven. It had a great taste. I precut the chicken into bite size pieces.

As per other reviews, I used pineapple juice in place of the broth, doubled the sauce ingredients except for the vinegar. I used Splenda instead of the sugar. Put some chopped pineapple in the baking dish with the browned chicken, put large strips of bell pepper over the chicken then poured the sauce over. Used 8 chicken tenders cut into bite sized pieces. Covered pan with foil and baked about 30 minutes. Turned out great. Served over white rice with a side of stir fry vegetables. Picky husband even asked for seconds, which emptied the pan so double the whole recipe for more than 2-3 people.

Pretty much kept to the recipe, our family loved the flavors
Easy to make. But the mixture poured over it while it baked in the oven made the bottom of the pieces soggy and the top got a bit dried out. Not crazy about the flavor, either.
Really favorable and easy to fix. Will make again.
Easy and i did not need to ask the family gave a “wow”.
This is a great recipe easy to follow and tastes soo good. JOHN FROM MI.
Vinegar flavor is very strong. Might try adding less next time.

The recipe, as written, had FAR too much vinegar. I'm glad I cooked the S&S sauce prior to putting it on the chicken. Small taste test, I couldn't possibly have eaten it. I ended up doubling the ketchup, and at least tripling the sugar. It was much better. After doctoring the recipe, the chicken was very good.
Turned out very good and came apart nicely when eating. Tasty and my parents like it.

Don’t get the rave reviews. I knew from the beginning it wouldn’t work. Pouring a cold mixture over hot fried meat is a recipe for an unpleasant dish. I will not make this again or recommend. It was also too vinegary and the chicken sitting in the cold sauce penetrated the chicken coating making it soggy. There are much better recipes out there for sweet and sour chicken.
